summary: Shu-chen Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang, having served as a teaching assistant there in 1996.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University, where she later served as professor (attested 2010). Her doctoral supervisor was Hans Henrich Hock, and she also studied under Chin-Fa Lien.

Shu-fen Liu works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She held posts at Academia Sinica (attested 2012) and served as a professor at its Institute of History and Philology (attested 2018).

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied under Shigeo Kamata and earned his BA at Komazawa University (~1961–1965), where he later served as a professor (attested 1988–2016).
Shudo Iwai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral coursework at Komazawa University. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1988).

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history and archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (~1919–1923) and Zhejiang University, later serving as director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1944–1982).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 2003), Bukkyo University (attested 2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2006), and Musashino University (attested 2006).

Shujun Motegi is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University (1973–1975) under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and earned an MA from Kyoto University (-1977). He later served as professor of ethics at Shinshu University (attested 2010).

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies at Komazawa University (~1970–1975). He worked at Komazawa University as a research assistant (~1973–1982) and professor (~1993–2017), and also held a post at Aichi Gakuin University.

Shuman Chen is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD from Northwestern University in 2014 under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, having also studied under traditional teacher Wei Chueh.

Shun'ei Hirai is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1949–1953) and the University of Tokyo (~1954–1959), later serving as a professor at Komazawa University (~1968–2000).
Shun'ei Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Otani University as a fixed-term assistant professor (-2013) and as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and became an emeritus professor at Taisho University (attested 1981–1982).
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic appointments at Shuchiin University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976).
Shunpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1940–1943) and later held a post there from ~1952 to 1984.

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Gyokujun So-on and Ian Kishizawa, and attended Komazawa University (~1926–1930). He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1958–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College (~1974–1999) and Shikoku University (~1999–2015, professor).
Shunshō Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1955) and later served as an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 1998–2006).
Shuntaro Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Ryukoku University in 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).
